LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 13.3.1 ‘WH’ QUESTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Language Use 13.3.1 ‘Wh’ questions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 13.3.1 ‘Wh’ questions, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: why’, ‘whom’ and ‘how’. Why is it important to ask questions correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 13.3.1 ‘Wh’ questions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is developed as they engage in meaningful question and

answer dialogues using Wh- questions appropriately.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with peers to practise using Wh- questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life-skills (Self-esteem): The learner acquires an elevated level of self-esteem as they gain the mastery of asking questions using the Wh- words.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the Wh- questions to seek information through asking questions in other learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
